card.saveHint: Lowering a value truncates tenants already configured above it (only affects runtime values; tenant rows are untouched and the numbers on tenant pages do not change). Takes effect immediately after saving.

card.invalidPositive: {label} must be an integer >= 1 (this setting does not support -1)

quota.intro1: Hard caps for every tenant: at runtime the smaller of the tenant value and the system value wins. Empty = use fallback, -1 = unlimited, 0 = nothing new may be created.
quota.intro2: Counting is by rows in the table regardless of status: deprecated / locked agents and skills still consume quota, and only deleting them frees it. Lowering a cap below current usage deletes nothing and disables nothing — the tenant simply cannot create more (remote imports are rejected too) until usage drops back under the cap. The "Fallback" column is the built-in default; it only applies when the system value is empty and is not editable.

flowConfigs.intro1: Hard caps for every tenant: at runtime the smaller of the tenant value and the system value wins. Empty = use fallback, -1 = unlimited.
flowConfigs.intro2: This group allows -1 (unlimited), unlike the "Agent run limits" group, which is all safety valves and has no -1. Also, for most entries 0 means "unset" and falls back to the parent level — write -1 to lift a limit, not 0.
flowConfigs.max_timeoutDesc: Upper bound for the total duration of a single run; the smaller of this and the flow instance's own timeout wins
flowConfigs.max_recursion_depthDesc: Call-stack depth across agents / flows, used to stop mutual recursion
flowConfigs.max_node_countDesc: How many nodes a single run may execute at most
flowConfigs.max_exec_countDesc: Total node executions allowed in a single run (loop unrolling adds up fast)
flowConfigs.max_loop_timesDesc: Iteration cap for loop nodes; long array traversal is truncated and logged
flowConfigs.max_run_recordsDesc: How many run records to keep per flow; the oldest are trimmed beyond that
flowConfigs.max_session_recordsDesc: How many memory records to keep per session; the oldest are trimmed beyond that

agentConfigs.intro1: Hard caps for every tenant: at runtime the smaller of the tenant value and the system value wins. Empty = use fallback.
agentConfigs.noNegativeOneTail: — all four entries are safety valves; setting them to "unlimited" tears the guard rails down.
agentConfigs.intro3: Session count and session storage are not in this group: they belong to resource quotas, see "Quotas" (those two allow -1 and can be overridden per user).

tenants.capTip: Platform-level gate: once closed, even if a tenant granted exec / browser to an agent, the tools are greyed out with a reason and the execution layer rejects them (not just a prompt-level hint). The browser keeps a Chromium alive and the exec family leaves long-lived processes, so the cost sits on the platform side. Egress (net.egress) is a cross-channel outbound policy: it depends on exec or shell being opened, and cannot be enabled when both are closed; with it closed, commands still run inside the sandbox but cannot reach the network. For domain-scoped outbound access use the flow's http node rather than this switch.
tenants.schemaTip: Discovered automatically and not editable: starting from t0 it counts up (t1, t2…) and takes the first free name. It re-checks before provisioning; if the name got taken you get a hint with a new value — confirm and submit again.
